categories.label: Before starting
categories.description: What you need to know before committing

items.q: How much does the entire process cost?
items.a: The cost varies by program. We confirm the exact amount in the initial consultation once we know your profile.

items.q: What's included in the price?
items.a: Airfare, accommodation in Paraguay, company incorporation costs, and minimum bank capital (varies by entity). We detail everything before starting.

items.q: What's NOT included?
items.a: Airfare, accommodation in Paraguay, company incorporation costs, and minimum bank capital (varies by entity). We detail everything before starting.

items.q: Can I pay in installments?
items.a: Yes. We work with a payment schedule linked to process milestones. For larger amounts, we agree on a personalized scheme.

items.q: Do I need to speak Spanish?
items.a: No. Our team speaks Spanish, English, Dutch, and German. We accompany you with simultaneous translation to each appointment.

items.q: Is the process fully legal?
items.a: Just one. The operational day is coordinated in a complete day.

items.q: How long does the entire process take?
items.a: We work on eligibility pre-screening before starting. If for any reason you are not eligible, we refund 80% of the payment as agreed in the contract.

items.q: How long does it take?
items.a: Absolutely. We work in strict compliance with Paraguayan law. We are registered with SEPRELAD as obligated subjects.

items.q: What happens if my residency is rejected?
items.a: The total time depends on the program. We confirm this during the initial consultation once we have reviewed your profile.

items.q: What types of residency exist?
items.a: Permanent residency (most common for Europeans), temporary residency (1 year, renewable), and investment residency (for investors with verifiable capital).

items.q: Can I bring my family?
items.a: Yes. Spouse and minor children can settle with you as dependents in your main application.

items.q: Can my children attend public school?
items.a: Yes. With a Paraguayan ID, minors access free public education. There are also private bilingual options (Spanish/English).

items.q: Do I need to apostille documents?
items.a: Yes. Documents from your home country must be apostilled (or legalized depending on country) to be valid in Paraguay.

items.q: How long does residency approval take?
items.a: Migraciones operates within a generous legal deadline; in practice, residency issuance moves briskly. We notify you as soon as it is ready.

items.q: Do I need to visit Migraciones multiple times?
items.a: No. A single visit on the operational day is sufficient for the residency and ID interviews. Everything else we handle.

items.q: What if my ID card takes a long time?
items.a: The Department of Identifications issues the ID card once the file is complete. We notify you and pick it up for you.

items.q: Can I open a bank account as a resident?
items.a: Yes. As a Paraguayan resident with ID, you can open a personal or business account at any local bank.

items.q: Which banks do Paraguayans use?
items.a: The main ones are Itaú, Continental, Sudameris, GNB, BNF (state-owned), and Visión. Each has slightly different requirements.

items.q: Do I need minimum capital?
items.a: It varies by bank. Some require an initial deposit, others do not. We guide you toward the best option for your profile.

items.q: Can I transfer money from Europe?
items.a: Yes. Paraguay has no exchange controls. You can receive international transfers without restrictions.

items.q: Do I need to declare the money I bring?
items.a: Yes, there are reporting requirements for significant amounts. For normal amounts, there is no limit. We guide you based on your case.

items.q: Do I need to incorporate a company?
items.a: Depends. If you only want to live in Paraguay with your foreign income, you do NOT need a company (Base program). If you want to operate locally or have an S.A., yes (Business or Investor).

items.q: What type of company is incorporated?
items.a: We recommend S.A. (Sociedad Anónima) or EAS (Empresa por Acciones Simplificada). We explain the differences in the consultation.

items.q: How much does it cost to incorporate an S.A.?
items.a: Depends on type and size. Includes notary fees and registration rates. We confirm the amount before proceeding.

items.q: What is the RUC?
items.a: Single Taxpayer Registry. It is your tax identification number. You need it if you will invoice or have employees.

items.q: What are the tax obligations?
items.a: Flat-rate regime on local income. If you only have foreign income, you do not pay local tax. We explain everything in the initial consultation.

items.q: Which tax regime suits me?
items.a: Depends on your situation. Individual, S.A., EAS, or monotributo have different advantages. We advise you.

items.q: Is it a good time to buy properties in Paraguay?
items.a: Paraguay's real-estate market remains in sustained growth. It is a good moment to evaluate options with local advice.

items.q: Can I buy as a foreigner?
items.a: Yes. Paraguay does not restrict property purchases by foreigners. With ID or RUC, the process is the same as for locals.

items.q: What areas do you recommend?
items.a: Depends on your style. For families: Villa Morra, Carmelitas, Loma Pyta. For nightlife: Paseo Carmelitas, Mariscal. For tranquility: San Bernardino (50 km away).

items.q: How much does a decent apartment cost?
items.a: The range is wide depending on zone and size. We help you evaluate options within your budget and needs.

items.q: Can I get a mortgage as a foreigner?
items.a: Yes, Paraguayan banks require a down payment. Some accept mortgages under accessible conditions. We accompany you in the evaluation.

items.q: How much does it cost to live in Paraguay?
items.a: The cost of living in Asunción is notably lower than in Western Europe. We cover concrete examples in the initial consultation based on your profile.

items.q: How is the health system?
items.a: There is IPS (public, basic coverage) and quality private hospitals (Sanatorio Migone, Sanatorio Italiano). We recommend private insurance.

items.q: Is there European community in Paraguay?
items.a: Yes. A vibrant multicultural community with Mennonite (German), Brazilian, Argentine, and growing Dutch/German communities, with presence in Asunción, Itapúa, Alto Paraná, and the Chaco.

items.q: Is Paraguay safe?
items.a: Asunción is one of the safest capitals in the region. Crime is low compared to other Latin American cities.

items.q: How is the climate?
items.a: Subtropical. Heat from October to March (25-40°C), cool from May to August (10-25°C). Winter is short and mild.

items.q: Do I need a car?
items.a: Recommended. Public transport in Asunción is limited. Used cars are accessible — we guide you toward reliable providers.

story.title: Sonia's story
paragraphs: Sonia is Paraguayan. She lived 7 years in the Netherlands, where she initially worked in the cleaning industry.

What was hardest about coming back was reinventing herself culturally. The paperwork was complicated, but the hardest part was rebuilding her life in a country that was both hers and foreign at the same time.
Nexa Paraguay is exactly that: almost-family accompaniment for European citizens who decide to live in Paraguay.

items.q: How long does the whole process take?
items.a: In-person filing: a single day. Residency and ID issuance follow the regular processing windows. We accompany you end to end.

items.q: How many trips do I need to make to Paraguay?
items.a: Our program is designed so that a single trip is sufficient for the operational day. After that, you only need to travel if you want to oversee the case in person or for personal matters.

items.q: What if a document is missing?
items.a: We detect it before your trip. Our pre-validation guarantees that you arrive in Paraguay with everything you need.

items.q: What happens if laws change during my process?
items.a: We monitor the regulatory environment and inform you immediately if there are changes that affect your case.

items.q: Is the process fully legal?
items.a: It is not necessary. Although the process is conducted in Spanish, we work with sworn translators and accompany you to every appointment.

items.q: What does the price include?
items.a: Professional fees, VAT, official rates, banking coordination, property tour (when applicable), and full accompaniment during the operational day.

items.q: What is NOT included?
items.a: International flights, accommodation, personal expenses, certified translations and apostilles in your country of origin.

items.q: How is payment made?
items.a: Pre-payment by bank transfer. No additional charges.

items.q: How much does it cost to maintain residency annually?
items.a: Annual maintenance of the residency permit is minimal. It includes the RUC renewal (tax registration), possible apostille renewals, and basic administrative steps. We guide you on the actual costs during the initial consultation based on your case.

items.q: Can I open a bank account as a foreigner?
items.a: Yes. It is the most complex process, but we prepare your financial profile and coordinate everything with the bank to maximize success.

items.q: What type of company is formed?
items.a: Our legal team recommends the most convenient corporate type (generally S.A. for liability protection). We explain the differences during the consultation.

items.q: Do you offer a bank account opening guarantee?
items.a: The final decision is the bank's. We guarantee professional preparation and coordination — if there are objective reasons for rejection, we help you with alternatives.

items.q: What happens after the first year (Investor)?
items.a: We propose a continuity plan that includes annual compliance, tax advisory, and any operational support your case needs.

items.q: Can I bring my family?
items.a: Yes. Each family member requires their own residency process. We coordinate cases together to maximize efficiency.

items.q: Can I keep my original citizenship?
items.a: Yes, Paraguay allows dual citizenship with most countries. You will not lose your original nationality.

items.q: How long can I be outside Paraguay without losing my residency?
items.a: Permanent residency requires you to be physically in Paraguay at least 1 day every 3 years. Temporary residency has more specific requirements — we explain them during the consultation.

items.q: What is the difference between permanent residency and citizenship?
items.a: Permanent residency allows you to live, work, and own property in Paraguay indefinitely, with the requirement of visiting at least 1 day every 3 years. Paraguayan citizenship requires 3 years of residency, renouncing your original citizenship (except for nationals of Spain, Italy, and a few other countries with bilateral agreements), and confers voting rights and a Paraguayan passport.

items.q: Can I work legally with the residency?
items.a: Yes, permanent residency allows you to work legally in Paraguay, whether as an employee or independently. You can also be a director or shareholder of companies without additional restrictions.

items.q: What happens if my residency application is rejected?
items.a: Residency applications are rarely rejected when properly prepared. In the unlikely event of rejection, we analyze the cause, address it, and refile the application. We provide continued support until your residency is approved.

# How to Open a Bank Account in Paraguay as a Foreigner

## Why open a bank account in Paraguay?

Paraguay offers a relatively straightforward banking system for foreigners who hold a cédula (national ID) or are in the process of obtaining residency. A local account lets you receive salaries, pay local services, conduct business in guaraníes, and integrate fully into the local economy.

## Requirements

- Valid passport (apostilled)
- Cédula paraguaya (or proof of residency application in process)
- Proof of address in Paraguay (utility bill or rental contract)
- Initial deposit (varies by bank, typically a relevant amount–500)
- Tax ID (RUC) for corporate accounts

## The major banks

The four main banks that work regularly with foreigners are **Banco Itaú Paraguay**, **Banco Continental**, **Banco Familiar**, and **BNF (Banco Nacional de Fomento)**. Each has different requirements and minimum balances.

## Step-by-step process

1. **Gather your documents**: passport, cédula or residency proof, proof of address, RUC if applicable.
2. **Choose your bank**: compare minimum deposits, monthly fees, and online banking quality.
3. **Visit a branch in person**: most banks require an in-person visit to open an account.
4. **Complete KYC (Know Your Customer)**: the bank will verify your identity and source of funds.
5. **Receive your debit card**: usually issued the same day or within 5 business days.

## What to expect

The process typically takes a personalized timeline from first visit to receiving your debit card. The bank will hold your initial deposit until KYC is complete.

## How Nexa helps

We coordinate the bank appointment as part of the operational day: from document preparation to walking you into the branch, we handle the legwork. Most of our clients leave Paraguay with a working local account, a corporate account for their S.A., or both.

complianceDisclaimer.title: Compliance Notice
complianceDisclaimer.content: Nexa Paraguay is a registered reporting entity before SEPRELAD (Superintendencia de Prevención de Lavado de Dinero). Our services comply with all applicable Paraguayan and international regulations, including AML/KYC requirements. All client relationships are subject to due diligence, including identity verification, source of funds verification, and beneficial ownership disclosure.
paragraphs: Nexa Paraguay does not provide legal, tax, or investment advice. The programs described are accompaniment services for immigration procedures, banking coordination, and real estate advisory — they do not replace the advice of a licensed attorney, tax advisor, or registered real estate broker.

Nexa Paraguay está registrada como sujeto obligado ante SEPRELAD (Secretaría de Prevención de Lavado de Dinero o Bienes) y aplica procesos KYC (Know Your Customer) conforme a las resoluciones vigentes.
Results depend on individual fulfilment of requirements and may vary. Information accurate as of the date of last update.

In real estate matters, Nexa Paraguay does not act as a real estate agent or property broker. We accompany people in the search, negotiation, and signing process, but all transactions must be formalized through a licensed escribano (notary) and, when applicable, a registered real estate broker.

seo.title: Glosario — Nexa Paraguay
seo.description: Términos clave: residencia permanente, cédula, RUC, IRE, territorialidad, SEPRELAD, KYC.

hero.headline: Glosario de términos clave
hero.subheadline: Clear definitions of the terms you will encounter during the process.

items.q: What is permanent residency?
items.a: Permanent migratory status in Paraguay. We handle the full process for you, including the in-person filing at Migraciones.

items.q: What is the national ID card?
items.a: Paraguay's national identification document, issued after residency is granted. It is the official ID document in Paraguay.

items.q: What is the RUC?
items.a: Single Taxpayer Registry. Tax identification number, equivalent to a European NIF. Required to operate legally with invoicing.

items.q: What is the IRE?
items.a: Corporate Income Tax. General rate on income generated in Paraguay. We apply the regime that best fits your situation.

items.q: What is the territorial tax system?
items.a: Tax system where only income generated inside the country is taxed. Paraguay taxes Paraguayan-source income, not foreign-source income.

items.q: ¿Qué es SEPRELAD?
items.a: Paraguay's anti-money-laundering authority. Nexa is a reporting entity, which means we comply with regulations on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing.

items.q: ¿Qué es KYC?
items.a: Know Your Customer. Identity and funds verification procedure used by banks and regulated entities before opening accounts or starting business relationships.

cta.title: ¿Tenés un término que no entendés?
cta.subtitle: Write to us. We'll add it to the glossary.

trust.title: What changes with a Dutch-speaking founder

items.title: Neerlandés nativo
items.description: Daily communication in Dutch. No translation friction.

items.title: Box 3 + emigratieheffing
items.description: We plan your move knowing exactly what the Belastingdienst will ask after you emigrate.

items.title: Cobertura CET + UTC-3
items.description: European-hour response from Amsterdam, on-the-ground execution from Asunción.

pillars.title: Territorial tax regime
pillars.description: Flat-rate regime on local income. Foreign income exempt. No currency controls. Compared with the worldwide-taxation regimes of Western Europe, it offers a structural fiscal architecture.

pillars.title: Vía migratoria real
pillars.description: Full residency, not just a digital-nomad visa. Suited for permanent fiscal residence once ties with the home country are properly unwound.

pillars.title: Fuera de la lista UE
pillars.description: Paraguay is not on the EU tax-haven list. Less friction with NL/BE banks when reporting the move.

items.q: How does Paraguay interact with box 3?
items.a: After emigration and severance of ties (woonplaatsverklaring), box 3 no longer applies. We coordinate what the Dutch tax office requires.

items.q: What happens with the emigratieheffing on a BV?
items.a: The exit tax applies to the unrealized capital gain in your BV at the moment of emigration. We help structure the move so you don't pay more than necessary.

items.q: Does Paraguay have a tax treaty with NL or BE?
items.a: No hay convenio bilateral en 2026, pero el sistema territorial de Paraguay lo hace innecesario en la mayoría de casos prácticos.

items.q: Can I keep my BV / BVBA after emigrating?
items.a: Yes, this is a common structure — Paraguayan residency + EU holding company for specific business lines.

seo.title: How it works — Nexa Paraguay
seo.description: Our 5-step process: choose services, parallel processing, operational day in Paraguay, ID and banking, settling in. From first call to your new life.

hero.headline: The Ideal Path to Residency
hero.subheadline: A streamlined collaboration between your country of origin and your new home in Paraguay.

process.title: A clear, structured process
process.totalDuration: Total time: depends on the program. We confirm this during the initial consultation.

steps.title: Choose your services
steps.description: Choose the specific support you need. We create a personalized document checklist and a fixed quote — no surprises.
steps.detailParagraph: During this initial phase, we have a free video consultation call where we understand your situation, your goals, and your timeline. Based on this, we propose the exact scope: residency only, plus company, plus banking, or the full package. You know exactly what you're paying before you commit.

steps.title: Parallel processing
steps.description: While you gather your documents at home, we begin work on the ground in Paraguay. We coordinate the legal preparation that would otherwise take months.
steps.detailParagraph: While you gather documentation in your country (birth certificate, police clearance, professional records), we begin work in Paraguay: legal preparation, company formation drafts, banking pre-qualification, and coordination with the local authorities. This parallel work is what makes our timeline realistic — we don't wait for you.

steps.title: Your day in Paraguay
steps.description: Travel to Paraguay with your documents ready. We accompany you to the in-person appointments and ensure every signature, copy, and seal is in place.
steps.detailParagraph: Your operational day starts early with our team. We pick you up and accompany you through each appointment: Immigration, Identifications, the bank, and any other step. We translate, we explain, we solve. By the end of the day, your key documents are filed and your case is in active processing.

steps.title: ID and financial activation
steps.description: Once your Paraguayan ID is issued, we activate your financial infrastructure. We open the bank account, register the RUC, and connect you to Paraguay's financial system.
steps.detailParagraph: When your ID is ready, we initiate financial activation: bank account opening, RUC registration, digital certificates, and any company-related steps. We prepare the documentation, coordinate with the bank, and accompany you through signing.

steps.title: Settling in and lifestyle
steps.description: With your legal and financial base in place, we help you settle in. This includes housing search, utility setup, school guidance if you have children, and discovering your neighborhood.
steps.detailParagraph: The final phase is the most rewarding: we help you find housing (rent or buy), set up utilities, register at schools if you have children, and discover your neighborhood. By the end, you don't just have a residence — you have a home.

highlights.title: The process in numbers
highlights.subtitle: What you need to know before starting.

items.title: Personalized timeline
items.description: Full accompaniment from consultation to ID card.

items.title: Bilingual team
items.description: Dutch, German, English, and Spanish — no intermediaries.

items.title: End-to-end coordination
items.description: Migraciones, notary, banking, RUC, and residency in a single flow.

faq.title: Questions about the process
faq.subtitle: The most common questions before starting.

items.q: How many trips do I need to make to Paraguay?
items.a: Our program is designed so that one trip is sufficient. The operational day is coordinated in one day.

items.q: How long does the entire process take?
items.a: The timeline depends on the program. We detail it during the initial consultation once we know your profile.

items.q: What happens if a document is missing?
items.a: We give you a personalized checklist before starting. If something is missing, we identify it in the initial consultation.

items.q: Do I need to speak Spanish?
items.a: No. Our team speaks Spanish, English, Dutch, and German. We accompany you to each appointment with simultaneous translation.

items.q: Can I bring my family?
items.a: Yes. Your spouse and minor children can settle with you as dependents.

items.q: What's included in the price?
items.a: Professional fees, government rates, certified translations, apostilles, in-person accompaniment, and initial tax advisory.

items.q: What's NOT included?
items.a: Airfare, accommodation in Paraguay, company incorporation costs, and minimum bank capital (varies by entity). We detail everything before starting.

items.q: What happens if my residency is rejected?
items.a: We work on eligibility pre-screening before starting. If for any reason you are not eligible, we refund the majority of the payment as agreed in the contract.

cta.title: Ready to start?
cta.subtitle: 30 minutes with Sonia or Luana. We tell you exactly how long, what you need, and how much it costs.

seo.title: Protección de datos — Nexa Paraguay
seo.description: Personal data protection policy and GDPR compliance of Nexa Paraguay.

hero.headline: Personal Data Protection Policy
hero.subheadline: Compliance with Paraguay Law 1682/01 and the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

items.q: What personal data do we collect?
items.a: Name, email, phone (optional), country, program of interest, and stated objective when you complete a form or contact us directly.

items.q: Do we collect sensitive data?
items.a: No. We never ask for racial origin, religion, sexual orientation, health, or political affiliation. If we need sensitive financial data, we request it via encrypted channels with your explicit consent.

items.q: How do we use your data?
items.a: Only to respond to your inquiry and, if you expressly authorize us, to send relevant information by email or WhatsApp about your move to Paraguay.

items.q: Do we share data with third parties?
items.a: CRM (HubSpot) and email provider (Mailchimp) under a data processing agreement. We never sell or share your data with third parties for commercial purposes.

items.q: How do I access, rectify, or delete my data?
items.a: Email us at paraguaynexa@gmail.com and we will respond within a maximum of 30 days (access, rectification, erasure, objection).

items.q: How long do you keep my data?
items.a: 24 months from the last contact, unless legally required.

items.q: Who can I complain to?
items.a: In Paraguay: National Directorate for Personal Data Protection (DINAPROD). In the EU: the supervisory authority of your country of residence.

hero.headline: Terms and Conditions
hero.subheadline: The rules of the game between you and Nexa Paraguay.

full.title: Key terms
full.subtitle: Executive summary. For the full version, contact us.

items.q: What is Nexa Paraguay?
items.a: A migration advisory firm based in Asunción. We offer residency services, bank account opening, company incorporation, and real estate due diligence.

items.q: Does Nexa provide legal or accounting services directly?
items.a: No. Nexa offers coordination, accompaniment, and administrative management services. Legal services are provided by independent attorneys registered in Paraguay.

items.q: What is the service area?
items.a: Paraguay. We operate from Asunción and accompany clients from anywhere in the world.

items.q: How do payments work?
items.a: 50% on signing the contract, 50% on receiving the Paraguayan ID card. For larger amounts, we agree on a personalized scheme.

items.q: When does a refund apply?
items.a: If Migraciones rejects your residency application, we refund 80% of the payment. The refund is processed within 30 business days.

items.q: What if I abandon the process?
items.a: If you abandon after the first payment but before starting, we retain 30% for administrative expenses. After started, no refund.

items.q: What is Nexa's responsibility?
items.a: To accompany you in coordinating the process with attorneys, notaries, accountants, and Paraguayan entities. We do not guarantee results from third parties (government approvals, banking decisions).

items.q: What is my responsibility as a client?
items.a: Provide true and complete documentation, attend coordinated appointments, and comply with Paraguayan legal requirements.

items.q: Is there a success guarantee?
items.a: No. Nexa is an accompaniment service, not a results guarantee. Times and approvals depend on Paraguayan entities.
